title: Phase A of w-prove-the-1-0-bar (clause-5 value demonstration): harvest >=3 REAL 'why did X happen' questions from this mission's own record (with a rejection log), source pre-World baselines from the record (UNMEASURED where it is silent), answer each by a timed provenance walk on a scratch worldd (session-gated commits of incident+evidence objects, log-range/object-get queries), verify every answer against independent ground truth outside World, land the comparison-table artifact at design_docs/verification/w-1-0-value-demonstration.md, and regression-guard it with one small host/daemon replay test

pre_registered.note: Two things are pre-registered here. (1) WHAT A FAILED WALK LOOKS LIKE: the honest-failure classes below are results (doc §4 — a demonstration that cannot fail demonstrates nothing); if World cannot answer a question the artifact records it and it counts as clause-5 evidence. (2) The mutation battery MU-1..MU-4, which runs AFTER the executor finishes M3 and snapshots .snap/M3/, against the landed tree — a controller/evaluator act, not executor work. Every arm: cp -p backup, sed with an asserted occurrence count, sha256 landed-proof (pre != post), a compile/vet assert BEFORE any test result is read, the scoped observable read (never the exit code alone), the named test required as the SOLE failure, then restore by cp from the .bak — restore asserted by shasum -a 256 equality AND test -x where a mode bit matters — and NEVER git checkout --.

failed_walk_classes.FAIL-TIME: the walk produced a verified answer but needed >300 s — recorded with the actual duration; counts as clause-5 evidence against the bar, never hidden
failed_walk_classes.UNVERIFIED: the walk produced an answer but no source outside World confirmed it — does NOT count toward the >=3 (doc §2)
failed_walk_classes.UNANSWERABLE: the walk could not produce the answer from the committed record — recorded as-is; substituting an easier question is forbidden
failed_walk_classes.NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT): the sandbox refused the loopback listener (PF-1) or both pty mint paths (PF-2) — labelled transport, never reported pass/fail; the M3 durability test stands as the regression guard and the block is reported as a finding
failed_walk_classes.PF-3: a live verification source is unavailable (gh/network down for Q2's fleet check; ailang.v0.30.0 removed) — fall back to the named in-git record as primary, mark the live check UNAVAILABLE; the answer counts only if an independent record still confirms it

pre_registered.runs_after: the executor finishes M3 and snapshots .snap/M3/
pre_registered.restore_discipline: cp -p <file> <file>.bak && sed -i '' ... <file>; <run scoped test>; restore cp <file>.bak <file>; restore asserted by shasum -a 256 <file> == pre-mutation digest AND test -x <file> where a mode bit matters; never git checkout --

doc_defects_found.summary: Row 78's ground truth cites scripts/mission_pi_run.sh:155; the live fleet file has the invocation at :165.
doc_defects_found.detail: Planner-measured via gh api 2026-09-24: the pi invocation sits at line 165 at fleet HEAD, still with zero -e flags and zero PI_FENCE_ROOT; issue sunholo-data/ailang#1043 is OPEN. Row 78 recorded :155 at iter-154 — correct then, drifted now.

doc_defects_found.summary: §4 says 'answer each by a provenance walk on World' but World has no semantic-ID query route; the walk entry point is a log-range scan.
doc_defects_found.detail: Planner-measured at base: GET /v1/objects/{ref} parses a hashref ONLY (handleObject), and POST /v1/commit cannot register names in epoch_registry_heads — its only writers are registry.Bootstrap, broker approve, and transitionreg. A walker must therefore scan log range and fetch each transitionRef object's metadata until the semanticId matches.
doc_defects_found.resolution: Recorded, doc NOT edited. The plan encodes the log-range scan as the walk's locate step and seeds artifact finding F-1 (proposed queue row w-object-lookup-by-semantic-id) — a finding, NOT scope (doc §9).

doc_defects_found.summary: Phase A's commit path is session-gated with a tty-fenced mint since a036062 (iter-181); the doc's Phase A mentions no credential setup.
doc_defects_found.detail: The doc was groomed 2026-09-21, before row 39 landed. POST /v1/commit now requires Authorization: Bearer <64-hex> resolved by the session middleware, and session mint refuses without a controlling terminal (os.OpenFile /dev/tty + y/N confirm).
doc_defects_found.resolution: Recorded, doc NOT edited. The plan's M4 carries the pty.spawn mint wrapper (with script -q /dev/null as alternate) and pre-registers NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT) if neither satisfies the fence.

features.name: Deterministic commit-fixture generator + checked-in commit JSON fixtures (one chained commit per question: incident object + evidence objects)
features.description: Write design_docs/verification/w-1-0-value-demonstration/gen_fixtures.py (~130 LOC, stdlib json/hashlib/base64/pathlib/argparse) carrying the FACTS table (slugs, questions, answers, evidence items quoted from the record per the plan's §2/§4 — never paraphrased) and emitting commits/q1-iter171-index-row.json, q2-iter154-unfenced-pi.json, q3-iter155-faithfulness-proof.json, and conditionally q4-iter181-ci-bench-401.json. Wire schema EXACTLY host/daemon/handlers.go commitRequest (decoder is DisallowUnknownFields): observedHead, objects[{hash,interfaceHash,semanticId,provenance,payload(base64)}], nextWorld{ref,revision,stateRoot,logHead}, entry{header{entryIndex,semanticsEpoch,transitionFn,interpreter,prevEntryHash,writtenBy},entryHash,transitionRef}. Q1 is genesis (observedHead ""; prevEntryHash a REAL sha256 — a zero prevEntryHash is writable but unreadable); successors chain observedHead/prevEntryHash. Every object hash == sha256:<hex> of the payload bytes (the store content-verifies). header.interpreter == sha256 of the live bytes of $HOME/.pinned-ailang/ailang, computed by the generator reading the binary (never hard-coded), so health's interpreter_ref matches at walk time (the replay pin). transitionRef = the incident object's hash; writtenBy/provenance = w-prove-1-0-phase-a. --check mode re-verifies everything from the emitted files.
acceptance_criteria: AC-M2-1 python3 design_docs/verification/w-1-0-value-demonstration/gen_fixtures.py --check -> rc=0 (recomputes every object hash == sha256 of the decoded payload; asserts exact top-level/object/header key sets; entryIndex 0..N contiguous; prevEntryHash chaining; interpreter == the pinned binary's current sha256).
AC-M2-2 ls design_docs/verification/w-1-0-value-demonstration/commits/q*.json | wc -l is 3, or 4 iff C4 was taken at M1 — and equals the harvest log's taken count.

AC-M2-3 grep -L 'w-prove-1-0-phase-a' design_docs/verification/w-1-0-value-demonstration/commits/q*.json prints nothing (every fixture carries the sprint provenance) and every semanticId is world/mission/{incident,evidence}/... .
G1 green (20 ok / 0 FAIL; verify_ail unchanged — no .ail).
Snapshot: generator + fixtures + the artifact copied into .snap/M2/ (cumulative — includes M1's file, full content).
traps: DisallowUnknownFields: any extra key anywhere (e.g. a 'kind' at top level, a 'name' on an object) makes the daemon answer 400 at replay — the generator must emit EXACTLY the schema keys and --check must assert the key sets.

Genesis prevEntryHash must be a REAL hash (sha256 of a fixed string), never the zero value — store.Commit writes it but store.GetLogEntry cannot read a zero back (TestGenesisRefLenienceIsExactlyOneField).
payload is base64 in JSON (Go []byte); hash is over the DECODED bytes — mismatching these is the classic fixture bug and MU-3's target.
Compute the interpreter ref from the pinned binary's live bytes; a hard-coded digest goes stale the day the pin bumps and the M4 replay-pin pre-check would fail opaquely.
Answer/excerpt strings come from the plan's FACTS verbatim — the executor never paraphrases the record into the fixtures.

features.name: host/daemon/value_demonstration_test.go — replay the checked-in fixtures through the real daemon stack and assert the walk queries return the recorded answers
features.description: One new Go test file (~140 LOC) in package daemon (reusing newHandlerDaemon, authHeader, and the existing httptest patterns — NO new package, so the suite stays 20 ok). It reads the checked-in fixtures from ../../design_docs/verification/w-1-0-value-demonstration/commits/, POSTs them in order through httptest.NewServer(d.Handler()) with the minted session header, then performs the walk IN-PROCESS: GET /v1/log?from=0, scan each entry's transitionRef, GET /v1/objects/<ref> metadata until the incident semanticId matches, GET ?payload=true and decode. TestValueDemo_AnswersMatchRecord: each taken question's incident object exists and its payload answer byte-equals the expectation table (killers MU-1, MU-3). TestValueDemo_EvidenceChainComplete: every hash in every incident's sources[] resolves via object get with a payload whose excerpt byte-equals the expectation table (killer MU-2). The expectation table is keyed by slug and mirrors the generator's FACTS verbatim.
acceptance_criteria: AC-M3-1 go test ./host/daemon/ -run 'TestValueDemo' -count=1 -v -> TestValueDemo_AnswersMatchRecord PASS: every taken question's incident object is located by semanticId and its answer byte-equals the expectation table. Killers: MU-1 (wrong expected answer), MU-3 (corrupted fixture payload).

AC-M3-2 same command -> TestValueDemo_EvidenceChainComplete PASS: every sources[] hash resolves via GET /v1/objects/<hash>?payload=true and its excerpt byte-equals the expectation table. Killer: MU-2 (evidence loop skipped).
AC-M3-3 G1 green with 20 ok / 0 FAIL (the test lands in the existing host/daemon package — no new package) and verify_ail.sh byte-identical (no .ail).
Snapshot: cumulative .snap/M3/ (M1+M2 files + the test). Executor STOPS here; the pre-registered mutation battery MU-1..MU-4 is the controller's next act.
traps: Reuse newHandlerDaemon/authHeader — do NOT re-mint through the CLI in-process and do NOT construct broker.Session (host/daemon is not a broker owner; the middleware boundary is the point).
The fixture path is ../../design_docs/... relative to the package dir (go test's working directory); an absolute path would break on any other rig.

The test asserts byte-equality against its own expectation table, not against strings re-derived from the fixtures — a test that reads its expectations from the subject under test is vacuous (MU-1 exists to prove this).
Order matters: POST q1 before q2 — observedHead chaining makes an out-of-order replay a 409, which the test treats as a fixture defect, not a daemon verdict.
Do not touch bench_test.go or any existing test; the only new symbol space is value_demonstration_test.go.

features.name: Live timed provenance walks on a scratch worldd (pty-minted session) + ground-truth verifications + artifact tables filled + walk transcript
features.description: Build the binary into .walk-scratch/ (untracked, EXCLUDED from snapshots), serve --db .walk-scratch/walk.db --bind 127.0.0.1:7654 --ailang-bin $AILANG_BIN, health + replay-pin pre-check (interpreter_ref == sha256 of the pinned binary), mint via printf 'y\n' | python3 -c "import pty,sys; pty.spawn(sys.argv[1:])" ... session mint --db ... --episode w-1-0-value-demo --grant fs.read=/tmp:1 --ttl 3600 --out .walk-scratch/token (alternate: script -q /dev/null), commit the fixtures in order via commit --file <f> --session $(cat token). Then per question, timer STARTS AT THE QUESTION: log range --from 0 -> object get per transitionRef until the incident semanticId matches -> object get --payload (base64 -d) -> follow every sources[] hash -> assemble the answer -> VERIFY against the plan's per-question ground-truth commands (ailang.v0.30.0 grep + git log -S for Q1; gh api fleet file + issue #1043 OPEN for Q2, with the PF-3 fallback; row-81/log-155 greps + git show --stat of the rebuilt row-59 split for Q3; git show a036062 bench diff + STATUS-181 grep for Q4) -> stop clock, record duration and verdict from the closed set {PASS, FAIL-TIME, UNVERIFIED, UNANSWERABLE, NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT)}. Fill the artifact's Timing/Verification/Comparison tables in the prescribed formats and append raw command output to walk-transcript.md. SIGTERM the daemon and record the drain line.
acceptance_criteria: AC-M4-1 every taken question has a Timing-log row with a verdict from the closed set and a numeric duration_s ('-' iff NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT)): grep -cE '\| (PASS|FAIL-TIME|UNVERIFIED|UNANSWERABLE|NOT-RUN)' <artifact> >= taken count, and grep -c "TBD" <artifact> == 0.
AC-M4-2 every PASS row has duration_s <= 300 (timer started at the question, doc §4.3) and its Verification row names a source OUTSIDE World whose command appears verbatim in walk-transcript.md.

AC-M4-3 the Comparison table carries the six prescribed columns (question, baseline method, baseline cost, walk time, verification source, verdict) with >=3 rows, and the harvest log WITH ITS REJECTIONS is present in the same artifact (doc §4.5 — the artifact is the deliverable).

AC-M4-4 G1 green; verify_ail.sh unchanged; the Findings section carries F-1 (semantic-ID query gap -> proposed queue row w-object-lookup-by-semantic-id) and F-2 (registry names not commit-settable) plus any fired PF-1/PF-2/PF-3 transport findings.
Snapshot: cumulative .snap/M4/ (M1–M3 files + the filled artifact + walk-transcript.md); .walk-scratch/ is EXCLUDED (untracked scratch). Executor STOPS here.
traps: The timer starts at the QUESTION, before the first query — starting it at the first successful query is the vacuity doc §4.3 names.
A verdict about binding the listener or satisfying the tty fence under sandbox is NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT) — label it, never report pass/fail (PF-1/PF-2).
Q1 verification must NOT run the current pin: v0.41.0 HAS the mission group (DEF-1). Use ailang.v0.30.0 and git log -S over the index.
Q2 verification asserts the PROPERTY (zero -e / zero PI_FENCE_ROOT), never row 78's :155 line number (DEF-2 drift; invocation is at :165 today).
Read-only git only (log/show/grep) — the executor runs NO git write operations; the controller commits from .snap/M4/.
Commit fixtures in filename order; a 409 HeadConflict means the chain or the order is wrong — fix the setup, never force a commit.
An answer only the walk confirms is UNVERIFIED and does not count toward the >=3 (doc §2) — say so in the table rather than upgrading it.

bands.work: M1 harvest log + record-sourced baselines + artifact skeleton
bands.driver: the harvest is prescribed (3 taken + C4 eligibility check + C5/C6 rejections); the executor re-reads and quotes rather than searches; the only real work is resisting imputation on the cost cells
the wire schema, genesis prevEntryHash lenience, and DisallowUnknownFields traps are all named with their source lines; the FACTS table is quoted from the plan, not authored

objections: All four baselines are expected UNMEASURED on cost: the record states method, not duration (doc §8 names this in advance). The comparison table's baseline-cost column will look empty; that is the honest measurement, and the baseline-METHOD column (with citations and recorded step counts) is what arms the ≤5-minute claim.

M4's four timed walks at ~0.15d assumes the listener binds and the pty mint works on this rig; if either fails the time is not spent — the verdicts flip to NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT) and the artifact records the block. The 0.35d is a cap either way.

top_risks: R-TRANSPORT — the executor sandbox refuses the loopback listener or the pty mint (PF-1/PF-2): the live walk flips to NOT-RUN(TRANSPORT), the M3 test stands as the regression guard, and the artifact records the block. Pre-registered; honest, but the sprint then demonstrates the walk in-process only — flagged for the controller to consider an attended re-run of M4's timed steps.
